Global Current Account Imbalances

Annual · USD billions · 2000–2026
Positive bars = surplus  |  Negative bars = deficit  |  US deficit shown as positive red line (sign reversed)  |  EM excludes China  |  Others = residual (advanced economies ex-US/Japan/UK/Euro Zone)  |  2024: IMF estimate  |  2025–2026: IMF projections

Current Account Imbalances vs. Net External Financial Positions

USD billions · Cumulative CAB (2009–2024) vs. net external position by instrument, 2024
Cumulative CA balance = sum of annual current account balances, 2009–2024  |  Net external position = 2024 stock, stacked by instrument: net FDI + net Portfolio (IMF CDIS/CPIS bilateral group matrices, intra-group flows excluded) + Reserves (World Bank/IMF IFS)  |  China’s gap narrows from about −$3.5T to about −$0.1T once reserves are added — its surplus sits overwhelmingly in reserves, largely invisible in bilateral FDI/Portfolio data  |  Sources: IMF WEO, CDIS, CPIS, World Bank/IMF IFS

Global Reserve Assets by Holder Group

USD billions · Monthly · January 2001–June 2025
Stacked by the same 7 groups used throughout this dashboard — built from the IMF's own pre-computed country and regional aggregates (IFS, RAFA_MV_USD)  |  EM ex-China — not China — is consistently the largest reserve-holding bloc  |  Navy line = world total  |  Source: IMF International Financial Statistics

Global Official Reserves: Currency Composition

USD billions · Quarterly · 2000-Q1–2025-Q3
Stack order (bottom→top): USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, CNY, Other reported currencies, Unallocated — gold deliberately excluded (a valuation, not a composition, story)  |  Dollar share has drifted from roughly two-thirds in the mid-2000s to just under 57% by 2025-Q3  |  Source: IMF COFER

Foreign Holdings of US Treasury Securities

USD billions · Monthly · March 2000–December 2025
Stacked by holder group (bottom→top): Japan, China Mainland, United Kingdom, Canada, India, Financial centers (Belgium/Luxembourg/Ireland/Switzerland/Cayman — the "custodial bias"/"Belgium bulge"), Other Asia/LatAm, All other  |  Japan overtook China as the top official holder around 2019  |  Source: US Treasury TIC (mfhhis01)

Global FDI Flow Map — 2024

USD billions · FDI stock positions (outward claims), all instruments · bilateral, by group
Each ribbon runs from the economy that holds the FDI claim (sender) to the economy where the investment is located (receiver)  |  Euro Zone = 20 euro-area members  |  EM ex-China = World minus the 41 IMF Advanced Economies minus China  |  Intra-group flows excluded  |  Source: IMF CDIS DIP 12.0.1 (2024 release)

Real Effective Exchange Rate

Click a region to select/deselect all

Source: BIS Effective Exchange Rate statistics (WS_EER), Real, broad basket  |  REER rises = appreciation; Invert flips that (10,000/REER) so a falling line = appreciation instead, matching the nominal-FX convention  |  Normalize rebases each line to 100 at the chosen date, for reading appreciation/depreciation since then.
